revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Choosing a Time-Capsule Box
revealWordProblem.text: Your class is choosing a box for the time capsule. The store sells three rectangular-prism boxes: a Small box that is 2 ft × 1 ft × 1 ft, a Medium box that is 2 ft × 1.5 ft × 1 ft, and a Large box that is 2 ft × 2 ft × 1.5 ft. Compute the volume of each box in cubic feet. Which box should the class buy if they need to fit at least 5 cubic feet of items? Explain how you decided.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Small: V = 2 × 1 × 1 = 2 ft³. Medium: V = 2 × 1.5 × 1 = 3 ft³. Large: V = 2 × 2 × 1.5 = 6 ft³. The class should buy the Large box because only its volume, 6 ft³, is at least 5 ft³.

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — How do we find volume when an edge is a fraction?
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. In this group we go deeper: trickier numbers, a second way to see it, and explaining why it works — not just getting the answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: A fractional edge does not change the rule: still multiply length × width × height — and you can explain why it works, even when it gets tricky.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: My capsule is 2 ft long, 1.5 ft wide, and 1 ft tall. I write V = length × width × height.
I put in the numbers: V = 2 × 1.5 × 1.
So the volume is 3 ft³. A fractional edge like 1.5 did not change my steps at all.

explore.instructions: Go deeper: Calculate the volume of each possible time capsule design. Use V = l × w × h. As you work, ask yourself WHY it works.

onLevel.stem: Two boxes: Box A is 10 × 5 × 4 inches. Box B is 8 × 6 × 5 inches. Which has more volume and by how much?
onLevel.explanation: Box A: 10 × 5 × 4 = 200 in³. Box B: 8 × 6 × 5 = 240 in³. Box B is bigger by 40 in³.
choiceFeedback: Recheck which box's volume is larger — recalculate both totals before comparing.
You picked the right box, but recheck the subtraction to find the exact difference.
These two volumes aren't equal — calculate each box's volume and compare the totals.
hints: This asks two things: which box holds more AND by how many cubic inches — so find both volumes first.
Compute each volume with V = l × w × h, then subtract the smaller total from the larger.
Box A: 10 × 5 = 50, then × 4. Box B: 8 × 6 = 48, then × 5. Compare the two totals.
onLevel.stemEs: Dos cajas: la caja A mide 10 × 5 × 4 pulgadas. La caja B mide 8 × 6 × 5 pulgadas. ¿Cuál tiene más volumen y por cuánto?
onLevel.explanationEs: Caja A: 10 × 5 × 4 = 200 in³. Caja B: 8 × 6 × 5 = 240 in³. La caja B es mayor por 40 in³.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Dimensions
workedExample.work: A box is 6 in long, 4 in wide, and 1/2 in tall.

workedExample.label: Calculate
workedExample.work: V = 6 × 4 × 1/2, and the student dropped the 1/2: V = 6 × 4 = 24 cubic in

onLevel.correctWork: The student ignored the fractional edge of 1/2 in. A fractional edge still counts: V = 6 × 4 × 1/2 = 24 × 1/2 = 12 cubic in.
hints: Check Step 3: did the student use the 1/2 in height in the multiplication?
A fractional edge does not change the rule. Multiply all three: 6 × 4 × 1/2 = 12 cubic in, not 24.
onLevel.explanation: The Calculate step threw away the 1/2 in height, but a fractional edge is still an edge. Multiply all three: V = 6 × 4 × 1/2 = 24 × 1/2 = 12 cubic in. A half-inch height makes the volume half of 24, not equal to it.
onLevel.explanationEs: En el paso de calcular se descartó la altura de 1/2 in, pero un lado fraccionario sigue siendo un lado. Multiplica los tres: V = 6 × 4 × 1/2 = 24 × 1/2 = 12 pulgadas cúbicas. Una altura de media pulgada hace que el volumen sea la mitad de 24, no igual a 24.

onLevel.stem: What is the volume of a prism with edge lengths 1/2 m, 3 m, and 4 m?
choiceFeedback: Adding the three edge lengths together won't give volume — multiply them instead.
Check the fractional edge — make sure you multiply by 1/2, not treat it as a whole number.
That's just one edge length — volume needs all three dimensions multiplied together.
hints: One edge is a fraction: 1/2 m. The other edges are 3 m and 4 m. The formula works the same with fractions.
Multiply all three edges: V = 1/2 × 3 × 4. Multiplying by 1/2 is the same as dividing by 2.
Multiply the whole numbers first: 3 × 4 = 12. Then take half of that result.
onLevel.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el volumen de un prisma con longitudes de arista de 1/2 m, 3 m y 4 m?

onLevel.stem: A cube has an edge length of 5 cm. What is its volume?
onLevel.explanation: A cube's volume is edge³ = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125 cm³.
choiceFeedback: Adding the edge three times won't give volume — multiply the edge by itself three times instead.
You squared the edge but forgot to multiply by it once more — a cube's volume needs edge × edge × edge.
Check your last multiplication — multiply the squared edge by the same edge length again.
hints: A cube's edges are all equal, so its length, width, and height are each 5 cm.
Use V = edge × edge × edge — multiply 5 by itself three times, not 5 × 3.
Start with 5 × 5 = 25, then multiply that result by 5 one more time.
onLevel.stemEs: Un cubo tiene una longitud de arista de 5 cm. ¿Cuál es su volumen?
onLevel.explanationEs: El volumen de un cubo es arista³ = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125 cm³.

extending.title: Find the Volume Error
hints: Check Step 3: what is 3 × 2.5?
3 × 2.5 = 7.5, not 5.5. The student may have added instead of multiplied.
extending.explanation: In the Calculate step, 3 × 2.5 was written as 5.5, which is what you get by adding 3 + 2.5 instead of multiplying. Three groups of 2.5 make 7.5, so V = 5 × 7.5 = 37.5 m³.
extending.explanationEs: En el paso de calcular, 3 × 2.5 se escribió como 5.5, que es lo que se obtiene al sumar 3 + 2.5 en lugar de multiplicar. Tres grupos de 2.5 dan 7.5, así que V = 5 × 7.5 = 37.5 m³.

extending.prompt: A toy company ships action figures in boxes that are 4 × 3 × 6 inches. A shipping crate is 24 × 12 × 18 inches. How many action figure boxes fit in the crate? Explain your reasoning step by step.
extending.sentenceFrame: Each toy box has a volume of ___ in³. The crate has a volume of ___ in³. I can fit ___ boxes because ___. I checked by ___.
extending.hint: Find three different factor combinations of the target volume.
hints: Two sizes matter: each toy box is 4 × 3 × 6 in and the crate is 24 × 12 × 18 in. Each crate edge is a multiple of a box edge.
Find both volumes, then divide the crate's volume by one box's volume. Check by counting rows, columns, and layers.
Start with one toy box: multiply 4 × 3 = 12, then multiply by 6. Next find the crate's volume the same way.
extending.explanation: Each toy box holds 4 × 3 × 6 = 72 in³ and the crate holds 24 × 12 × 18 = 5184 in³, so 5184 ÷ 72 = 72 boxes fit. The division comes out exact because every crate edge is a whole-number multiple of a box edge: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 across, 12 ÷ 3 = 4 deep, and 18 ÷ 6 = 3 layers, and 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 confirms it.
extending.explanationEs: Cada caja de juguete tiene 4 × 3 × 6 = 72 in³ y la caja grande tiene 24 × 12 × 18 = 5184 in³, así que caben 5184 ÷ 72 = 72 cajas. La división sale exacta porque cada lado de la caja grande es un múltiplo entero de un lado de la caja pequeña: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 a lo ancho, 12 ÷ 3 = 4 de fondo y 18 ÷ 6 = 3 capas, y 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 lo confirma.

extending.stem: A fish tank measures 2 1/2 ft by 2 ft by 3 ft. What is its volume?
choiceFeedback: You multiplied two dimensions but left out the third edge length.
Check the fractional edge length — rounding it down changes your answer.
Double check your multiplication — recompute each step to avoid doubling the result.
hints: One dimension is a mixed number: 2 1/2 ft. Rewrite it as 2.5 before multiplying.
Use V = l × w × h with all three numbers: 2.5 × 2 × 3. Keep the half — don't round it away.
Multiply the easy pair first: 2 × 3 = 6. Then multiply that result by 2.5.
extending.stemEs: Una pecera mide 2 1/2 ft por 2 ft por 3 ft. ¿Cuál es su volumen?

extending.stem: A prism with a 3/4 ft by 2 ft base has a volume of 9 ft³. What is its height?
choiceFeedback: Recalculate the base area first (3/4 × 2), then divide the volume by that.
That's the volume given, not the height — divide it by the base area to find height.
Make sure you find the full base area — multiply both base dimensions before dividing.
hints: You know the volume (9 ft³) and the base dimensions (3/4 ft and 2 ft). The height is missing.
Height = Volume ÷ base area. Find the base area first, then divide the volume by it.
Base area: 3/4 × 2 = 1.5 ft². Now ask what number times 1.5 equals 9.
extending.stemEs: Un prisma con una base de 3/4 ft por 2 ft tiene un volumen de 9 ft³. ¿Cuál es su altura?
extending.explanationEs: Altura = V ÷ (área de la base) = 9 ÷ (3/4 × 2) = 9 ÷ 1.5 = 6 ft.

extending.stem: A time-capsule box measures 6 in long, 4 in wide, and 3 in tall. What is its volume?
extending.explanation: V = length × width × height = 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 cubic in. Volume uses cubic units.
choiceFeedback: Are you adding the dimensions? Volume multiplies all edges: length × width × height.
You multiplied two dimensions but forgot the third — include length, width, AND height.
Check the units — this fills 3D space, so it needs cubic units, not square units.
extending.stemEs: Una caja para una cápsula del tiempo mide 6 in de largo, 4 in de ancho y 3 in de alto. ¿Cuál es su volumen?
extending.explanationEs: V = largo × ancho × alto = 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 pulgadas cúbicas. El volumen usa unidades cúbicas.
hints: Volume measures the space inside a solid, and it is always labeled in cubic units.
Use V = length × width × height: multiply two of the dimensions first, then multiply by the third.
Start with 6 × 4 = 24. Now multiply that result by the height of 3.
hintsEs: El volumen mide el espacio dentro de un cuerpo y siempre se escribe en unidades cúbicas.
Usa V = largo × ancho × alto: multiplica primero dos de las dimensiones y luego multiplica por la tercera.
Empieza con 6 × 4 = 24. Ahora multiplica ese resultado por la altura de 3.

extending.stem: Two storage boxes are ready to pack. Box A is 5 × 5 × 2 inches and Box B is 4 × 4 × 3 inches. Which box holds more?
choices: Box A, because 50 cubic in is more than 48 cubic in
Box B, because 48 cubic in is more than 50 cubic in
Box B, because it is taller
extending.explanation: Box A: 5 × 5 × 2 = 50 cubic in. Box B: 4 × 4 × 3 = 48 cubic in. 50 > 48, so Box A holds more.
choiceFeedback: Compare the two volume numbers again — which one is actually larger?
The two boxes have different volumes — calculate each one and compare the totals.
Height alone doesn't decide which holds more — compare the full volumes instead.
extending.stemEs: Hay dos cajas de almacenamiento listas para empacar. La caja A mide 5 × 5 × 2 pulgadas y la caja B mide 4 × 4 × 3 pulgadas. ¿Cuál caja guarda más?
extending.explanationEs: Caja A: 5 × 5 × 2 = 50 pulgadas cúbicas. Caja B: 4 × 4 × 3 = 48 pulgadas cúbicas. 50 > 48, así que la caja A guarda más.
hints: How much a box holds is its volume, not its height or its widest side.
Find the volume of each box separately with V = l × w × h, then compare the two numbers.
For Box A, 5 × 5 = 25, then multiply by 2. Do the same kind of work for Box B before comparing.
hintsEs: Lo que cabe en una caja es su volumen, no su altura ni su lado más ancho.
Halla el volumen de cada caja por separado con V = l × w × h y luego compara los dos números.
Para la caja A, 5 × 5 = 25 y luego multiplica por 2. Haz el mismo trabajo con la caja B antes de comparar.

extending.stem: A keepsake box is 4 in long, 3 in wide, and 1½ in tall. What is its volume?
extending.explanation: V = 4 × 3 × 1.5 = 12 × 1.5 = 18 cubic in. A fractional edge does not change the steps.
choiceFeedback: Are you adding the dimensions? Volume multiplies all edges: length × width × height.
You found the base area but forgot to multiply by the height for volume.
Double check the height value — using the wrong height changes your answer too much.
extending.stemEs: Una caja de recuerdos mide 4 in de largo, 3 in de ancho y 1½ in de alto. ¿Cuál es su volumen?
extending.explanationEs: V = 4 × 3 × 1.5 = 12 × 1.5 = 18 pulgadas cúbicas. Una arista fraccionaria no cambia los pasos.
hints: A fractional edge length works exactly like a whole-number one — the formula V = l × w × h does not change.
Multiply the two whole-number edges first, then multiply that product by the fractional height.
4 × 3 = 12. Now multiply 12 by 1½, which you can split into 12 × 1 plus 12 × ½.
hintsEs: Una arista fraccionaria funciona igual que una entera: la fórmula V = l × w × h no cambia.
Multiplica primero las dos aristas enteras y después multiplica ese producto por la altura fraccionaria.
4 × 3 = 12. Ahora multiplica 12 por 1½, que puedes separar en 12 × 1 más 12 × ½.

extending.title: Level 2 Extension — Catch the Packing Mistake

workedExample.label: Dimensions
workedExample.work: A box is 7 in long, 3 in wide, and 2 in tall.

extending.correctWork: The student only multiplied length × width and forgot the height. V = 7 × 3 × 2 = 21 × 2 = 42 cubic in.
hints: Check Step 3: did the student use all three dimensions?
Volume needs length × width × height. Multiply 21 by the height of 2 to get 42 cubic in.
extending.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2: Descubre el error de empaque
extending.explanation: The Calculate step used only the length and width and never brought in the 2 in height — that is area thinking, not volume. All three edges must multiply: V = 7 × 3 × 2 = 21 × 2 = 42 cubic in.
extending.explanationEs: En el paso de calcular solo se usaron el largo y el ancho, y nunca se incluyó la altura de 2 in; eso es pensar en área, no en volumen. Los tres lados deben multiplicarse: V = 7 × 3 × 2 = 21 × 2 = 42 pulgadas cúbicas.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Volume of Rectangular Prisms is rounding a fractional edge length to the nearest whole number before multiplying, instead of using the exact fraction or decimal. For a box that is 2 ft × 1.5 ft × 1 ft, a student might round 1.5 down to 1 and compute 2 × 1 × 1 = 2 ft³, but the correct volume uses the exact edge length: 2 × 1.5 × 1 = 3 ft³ — a full cubic foot larger. Before you submit, ask: 'Did I multiply using the exact fractional or decimal edge length, or did I round it off first?'

questions.stem: What is the volume of a rectangular prism with l = 7 in, w = 3 in, h = 4 in?
questions.explanation: V = l × w × h = 7 × 3 × 4 = 84 cubic inches.

questions.stem: Which unit is used for volume?
questions.explanation: Volume measures 3D space, so it uses cubic units like in³. Square units (in²) are for area, and inches are for length.
